speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, please describe your current symptoms in detail, specifically regarding the increasing pain and swelling in your right knee, and tell me about the episodes of pain during urination. You also mentioned a history of a swollen left ankle; did that episode involve any skin changes or fever before it resolved?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive Arthritis (Reiter's Syndrome). The clinical picture of asymmetric oligoarthritis (knee and ankle), urethritis, sexual activity, and family history of autoimmunity is highly suggestive. I am requesting a Urinalysis, HLA-B27, and joint fluid analysis to confirm.
